content.text:
**Finding submitted: deviation (INDEMN)**

- **What exists:** Section 6.3 contains a genuine counterparty indemnity — Cellco as Servicer (p0291) and as Marketing Agent (p0292) indemnifies the Issuer, Owner Trustee and Indenture Trustee for third-party claims, damages and defence costs, backed by a standard notice / assumption-of-defence / settlement-consent procedure (p0293–p0295), survival (p0296–p0298) and a repayment mechanic (p0299). There is no offsetting one-way indemnity from our side; p0372 is only a narrow Depositor defend-title covenant, which is acceptable.
- **Why it still fails the fallback:** the trigger is confined to Cellco's *willful misconduct, bad faith or gross negligence* (mirroring the Section 6.2(a) liability standard). There is no IP infringement indemnity at all — which the rule's detection guidance treats as a deviation even at fallback — and no cover for Cellco's failure to comply with Law or for unauthorized access to/disclosure of Obligor data, both live exposures given Cellco's consumer-facing servicing and custody of Obligor personal data.
- **Redline (validated ok:true):** a new Section 6.3(a)(iii) inserted after p0292 adding IP-infringement, breach-of-Law and data-breach prongs, expressly untethered from the willful misconduct/bad faith/gross negligence standard, with all existing procedure and survival mechanics left intact. Fallback offered in the comment: narrowing the IP prong to materials and systems Cellco supplies.
